The packet w02b-p15-059 reader_evidence carries the same stale hash. All 51 exact_current_text strings still match the files verbatim.

The closing caveat 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general' is supported only by the annex scope sentence (annex lines 103-104). No instance is exhibited and there is no pointer to the reparameterization example of thm:p15-bayes-transformation (bayesian-updating-prediction.tex 313-319). Read here as a definitional scope remark, not an owed proof; a one-line cross-reference would settle it.

The clause 'if c=0, a smaller size can attain the same power' rests on one informal sentence. The witness 1{f1>0}, whose size P0(L>0) is below alpha whenever alpha > P0(L>0), is implied but not written.

Existence of j with P(K>j) <= alpha <= P(K>=j) is presupposed by 'choose' and used in the C008 proof (annex 196-211) without a written argument. It follows from monotonicity of the finite tail, or from thm:p15-likelihood-threshold through the monotone ratio.

Mirror-image sub-steps are delegated by wording: line 445 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)', line 593 'Similarly for k<n', line 690 'Likewise F_{n,p}(k)=1-I_p(k+1,n-k)'. Each has a fully written twin immediately before it, so these were not scored as unwritten proofs.

The constant-term agreement in the completed-square identity is asserted ('agree after putting them over tau^2 s^2 (tau^2+s^2)') rather than displayed. The theta^2 and theta coefficients are verified explicitly.

'A finite tagged union of standard Borel spaces is standard Borel' is asserted without proof or reference. It is not load-bearing, since thm:p15-bayes-posterior-kernel needs only a measurable parameter space.

Source wording: the first Jeffreys and K&R label is paraphrased as 'negligible mention' (source: 'Not worth more than a bare mention', K&R p.777). K&R eq.(16) also uses alpha_k for prior odds against H_0, whereas this chapter's alpha_k are prior model probabilities, and no notation note is given (contrast the explicit note on Neyman's alpha at hypothesis-tests-and-confidence.tex 258-260).

NP 1933 p.300 extends the boundary condition (24) from the patch s_1 'consequently at every point on the complete boundary S'. The handbook states and proves only the local patch version, which is what its own wording promises.

NP 1933 pp.295 and 301 (the likelihood principle lambda, eqs.(11)-(14), and its relation to best critical regions) fall inside the cited locator pp.293-301 but are not represented by any of the 18 queue components. They are outside this audit's owed list.
